knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 5.1.7
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly outlines how a Bayesian credibility approach uses prior and data to produce a credibility premium in a simple case?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Bayesian credibility requires prior-to-posterior structure that justifies μ and Z. Empty formula or EB conflation are wrong.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Prior, update to posterior, credibility premium Z X̄ + (1-Z) μ from structure.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Writing the blend formula without a Bayesian warrant or collapsing into Empirical Bayes.

choices.label: Specify a prior or structural distribution for risk parameters; update with data to a posterior; in a simple case the credibility premium takes the form Z times X̄ + (1 minus Z) times μ with Z and μ determined from the prior structure.
Write Z times X̄ + (1 minus Z) times μ with no Bayesian story; the blend formula alone defines Bayesian credibility.
Applying Bayesian credibility finishes the Empirical Bayes approach because both yield a numeric premium.
Bayesian credibility uses only the sample mean X̄ with Z = 1 always; the prior enters only in Empirical Bayes.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 5.1.7
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. In a simple Bayesian credibility setup with known structural parameters, the credibility premium takes the form Z times X̄ + (1 minus Z) times μ. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: State what prior supplies; refuse EB conflation.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Known structural parameters from prior theory yield mu and Z. EB estimates structural parameters from collective experience.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Prior supplies mean and variance components for mu and Z. EB estimates structurals from data.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Accepting Bayesian credibility as finishing Empirical Bayes.

choices.label: The prior or known structural distribution supplies the overall mean and variance components so mu and Z are determined theoretically, then combined with observed X̄. Empirical Bayes estimates those structural parameters from data; a different approach from treating them as known in the Bayesian calculation.
Applying Bayesian credibility finishes the Empirical Bayes approach.
mu and Z must be estimated from collective data even in the fully Bayesian setup; prior structure supplies nothing.
Structural parameters are always user-chosen constants unrelated to any prior; Z equals 1 by definition.

worked_example.title: Bühlmann Z from prior structure, then premium
worked_example.problem_statement: In a Bayesian credibility (Bühlmann) setting, the expected process variance is EVPV = 200 and the variance of hypothetical means is VHM = 50, so k = EVPV/VHM = 4. A risk has n = 8 observation years with X̄ = £950 and hypothetical mean μ = £800. Compute Z = n/(n+k) and the Bayesian credibility premium.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Form Z = n/(n+k) before the premium convex combination.

steps.label: Credibility factor
steps.explanation: Bühlmann credibility increases with more years and decreases with larger k.

steps.label: Bayesian credibility premium
steps.explanation: With Z in hand the premium is the usual credibility mixture.

steps.label: Link to prior structure
steps.explanation: Here k is known from the prior structure (EVPV and VHM), not estimated from the collective sample.

worked_example.common_pitfall: Using Z = k/(n+k), or estimating k from the single risk's sample variance instead of using the given EVPV/VHM.
